evals.name: case-report-azmi-sharom
evals.prompt: I need a case report for COM741 on Public Prosecutor v Azmi Sharom [2015] 6 MLJ 751, the Federal Court decision on whether the Sedition Act 1948 is constitutional. ILAC per issue, then the Discussion with a comparative table. Around 2,000 words.
evals.expected_output: Mode A case report: case details, material facts, one ILAC block per issue, ratio stated as a rule and obiter identified, outcome, Discussion with theory, comparison table and critique, APA 7 references, study-only disclaimer.

evals.name: incident-report-fahmi-reza
evals.prompt: Write an incident report on the Fahmi Reza clown caricature of Najib Razak (2016) and his prosecution under section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act. Was the prosecution lawful and constitutional? Include what has happened since, and how s.233 has changed.
evals.expected_output: Mode B incident report: timeline with confirmed vs alleged facts, stakeholders, ILAC per issue, current status with date checked, s.233 amendment flagged, Discussion, APA 7 references, disclaimer.

evals.name: scenario-tiktok-religion-osa
evals.prompt: Lecturer's scenario for our media law tutorial: a Kuala Lumpur TikTok influencer posts a video mocking a religious group's practices. It goes viral. Police open an investigation under Penal Code s.298A and CMA s.233, and MCMC directs TikTok to remove the video. Analyse the legal position of the influencer and of TikTok. The brief says 1,500 words maximum and the Discussion must use only one theoretical framework.
evals.expected_output: Hypothetical treated as an incident report; separate analysis for influencer and platform; current law (grossly offensive threshold, Online Safety Act 2025 in force) flagged; brief's word limit and single-theory rule followed.
